fatal_errors: The proposed Cr-Mo-W-modified equiatomic HEA is not the studied AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
The response replaces the actual comparison with DS2205 and thermal-shock/immersed reciprocating tests with an unspecified high-temperature oxidation experiment.

It attributes performance primarily to a refractory-element-derived high-temperature oxide scale, whereas the target mechanism involves retained L12/B2 lamellae, aqueous passivation and repassivation, and temperature-dependent tribo-layer stability.
The specified 15% Cr, 15% Mo, and 10% W composition and claimed benefits have no cited or supplied evidence.
It does not identify the nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and increased tribo-layer disruption at 100 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad topic of improving HEA tribo-corrosion resistance and offers a controlled, falsifiable comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target material, intervention, comparator, or conditions. Its only mechanistic overlap is the generic idea that a protective surface film can reduce corrosion and wear. The target instead concerns as-cast lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 versus duplex stainless steel 2205 in deionized water at 25–100 °C after rapid thermal cycling, with superior behavior linked to phase retention and robust repassivation. The proposed refractory alloy may be an independently testable concept, but its composition, oxide-scale mechanism, and expected superiority are unsupported here.
